source_read: PMC HTML, PMC2911490 (accepted author manuscript): abstract, Introduction, Method, Results, Tables 1-5 (HTML), Discussion and acknowledgments read in full; Figures 1-3 (images) read from legends and text only.

claims.overstatement: The comparison is confounded in a way the claim does not mention: 48 of 83 methamphetamine-dependent participants (56-59%) had HIV and 28-32% had hepatitis C, while all controls were HIV- and HCV-negative by design; HIV itself is associated with neurocognitive impairment. Also, only the non-abstinent subgroup differed significantly from controls (38% vs 16%, p=0.03); the abstinent subgroup's 24% did not.
claims.note: 34% is printed in the Discussion ('about 34%' of the methamphetamine-dependent sample impaired at baseline) and matches the pooled Table 1 figures (6/25 + 22/58 = 28/83 = 33.7%); controls 16% (6/38) in Table 1. Impairment = global deficit score >0.5 (about T<40, 16th percentile), which the authors call relatively liberal but validated. Baseline group means support the 'low-average to average' part: global T 47.1 and 46.2 in the two user groups vs 50.1 in controls; domain means 44.3-49.0 (Table 3).

anchors.locator: Table 1 ('NP at baseline (% impaired)'); Discussion, para 3
anchors.extracted: Baseline impairment by GDS >0.5: abstinent 24% (6/25), non-abstinent 38% (22/58), controls 16% (6/38), p=0.049, non-abstinent > controls (p=0.03); abstinent vs controls and abstinent vs non-abstinent n.s. Discussion: about 34% of the methamphetamine-dependent sample impaired at baseline.
Global T (mean, SD): abstinent 47.1 (5.1), non-abstinent 46.2 (6.1), controls 50.1 (5.2), F=5.70, p=0.004; domain means in users 44.3 (motor, non-abstinent) to 49.0 (working memory).

HIV in 56% and 59% of the two user groups and HCV in 28% and 32%, none in controls; users abstinent at least 10 days (typically 1-2 months) at baseline; GDS cut-off 0.5 described as relatively liberal (Discussion, final para).

claims.overstatement: None for the main statement. One nuance on 'so did 6 controls impaired at baseline': true for the global score (impaired controls +3.3 T, 43.70 to 47.01, vs impaired abstainers +6.7 T, 41.26 to 47.94; in baseline-SD units about 1.65 vs 1.73), consistent with regression to the mean, but not for the domains where the paper's interaction was found: speed of information processing (impaired controls -1.4 T vs impaired abstainers +8.2 T; three-way interaction p=0.014) and motor (-0.1 vs +9.7 T; p=0.051). The claim should not imply that the whole subgroup finding is explained by the impaired controls.
claims.note: All numbers from this source match: 25 abstinent, 58 non-abstinent, 38 controls; mean interval 13 months (SD 5.6, range 6-42); time effect F(1,118)=55.12; group x time p=0.126 (printed as F(2,188)=2.11 - the denominator df is inconsistent with 121 participants, but p is the same for df 118); abstainer-control global gap 3.0 T at baseline (47.1 vs 50.1) and 2.7 T at follow-up (50.1 vs 52.8). Abstinence classification was by self-report (no biological verification during the interval, a limitation the authors state).

anchors.locator: Results > Global Cognitive Functioning and Individual Cognitive Domains, para 1; Tables 3-4
anchors.extracted: All groups improved: time F(1,118)=55.12, p<0.01; no group x time interaction, F(2,188)=2.11, p=0.126. Global T baseline: abstinent 47.1 (5.1), non-abstinent 46.2 (6.1), controls 50.1 (5.2); follow-up 50.1 (3.6), 47.8 (6.3), 52.8 (5.1). Abstainers no longer significantly different from controls at follow-up (gap 2.7 vs 3.0 T at baseline) but still worse on working memory and executive functions.

Time x group x baseline impairment: global F(2,115)=2.88, p=0.061 (trend); impaired abstainers (n=6) +6.7 T (d 1.73, t=3.66, p=0.015); impaired controls (n=6) +3.3 T; impaired non-abstainers (n=22) +2.0 T. Speed of information processing interaction F(2,115)=4.45, p=0.014 (impaired abstainers +8.2 T; impaired controls -1.4 T); motor F(2,115)=3.06, p=0.051 (+9.7 vs -0.1 T).

Interval 13 months on average (SD 5.6, range 6-42); 'abstinent' = no self-reported methamphetamine use over the interval; no biological verification of use during the interval; small samples; authors emphasise trends.

claims.note: The data support the claim's 'not shown to change with abstinence more than practice effects do' (no significant group x time interaction; all groups improved). The authors' own conclusion runs further ('partial recovery ... may extend beyond a year'), resting on a change in significance status (gap 3.0 to 2.7 T) and on a 6-person subgroup. In this sample education did not differ significantly (12.4, 12.7 vs 13.4 years, p=0.159) and premorbid reading was a trend (p=0.075); the main between-group differences in risk factors were HIV/HCV, other substance use and psychiatric history (bipolar disorder in 20% of abstainers).

anchors.locator: Results para 1; Discussion paras 2 and 5; Table 1
anchors.extracted: Group x time p=0.126 with a large overall time effect; authors acknowledge practice effects and include a retested control group; no measure before methamphetamine use; education p=0.159, WRAT-3 reading 97.6/99.3 vs 103.7 (p=0.075); HIV 56-59% vs 0%, HCV 28-32% vs 0%.

key_findings.correction: Recalculation confirmed: Student t=2.30, df 61, p=0.025 (Welch p=0.017); with the three-group pooled error (LSD) p=0.058.
Also recomputed: in baseline-SD units the impaired controls' global gain (3.31 T) is d=1.65, close to the impaired abstainers' 1.73.
Recomputed d with baseline SD: 1.26; impaired controls -0.34.

reporting_issues.note: Recomputed: follow-up Student p=0.025, Welch 0.017, LSD 0.058; baseline Student 0.028, LSD 0.041.
Impaired controls: 3.31 T, d 1.39 (RMS SD) / 1.65 (baseline SD).
Pairwise WRAT-3 recomputed: abstinent vs controls p=0.028, non-abstinent vs controls p=0.035 (Student).

Reference list checked: 2001a = J Neurosci 21:9414 (DAT recovery), 2001b = Am J Psychiatry 158 (psychomotor impairment). The cross-card statement about other first-pass cards was not checked (outside this reader's sources).

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E very high for the abstinence-related change estimates and high for baseline user-control contrasts agreed.

missed: For cl_meth_cognition_normal_range: the 34% vs 16% contrast should carry the HIV confound (56-59% of users HIV-positive, controls HIV- and HCV-negative by design); the card records the HIV prevalence (KF15) but the claim that cites the 34% figure does not mention it.

For cl_meth_cognition_abstinence: the impaired-control comparison holds for the global score but not for processing speed and motor, the domains with the reported interactions (impaired controls -1.4 and -0.1 T vs impaired abstainers +8.2 and +9.7 T); the card has the numbers (KF9-10) but the claim's 'so did 6 controls' could be read as covering all domains.
